name: Reptile House
label: Dischord
lede: Reptile House was Baltimore's answer to D.C.: a singer who'd turn into Daniel Higgs, a drummer who'd land in Samhain, and a debut 7" that sat out of print for a quarter century.

eras.title: Forty miles up the road from D.C.
eras.text: D.C. had Dischord and a scene with a name. Baltimore had the Marble Bar, Jules Club House and a handful of kids. Reptile House grew into the city's leading hardcore band, per AllMusic, bolting D.C. drive and California punk onto darker imagery and psychedelic guitar.

years.h: Goldsborough and Strasser, high school friends, start Reptile House
years.p: [[Joe Goldsborough|279792ca-9410-4c9c-96e9-aad841c43f05]] plays guitar and Daniel V. Strasser, later [[Daniel Higgs|6dd4abcc-0321-4ac0-b3bf-0a9422c450d9]], sings. AllMusic's original lineup adds David Rhodes on bass and [[London May|57e0394c-afeb-4021-8193-940084dd4717]] on drums.

years.h: The first record is a flexi-disc tucked into Testube zine
years.p: Two Reptile House songs, self-released, ride along inside the zine, per Wikipedia.

years.big: The whole [Baltimore] hardcore scene couldn't believe the Sun devoted a full front page.
years.src: Maryland Center for History and Culture
years.h: Reptile House makes the front page of the Sun
years.p: At the New Loft, Joseph Kohl photographs Reptile House singer Daniel Strasser sharing the mic with a kid in the crowd, Anthony "Toad" Brennan, while Joe Goldsborough plays guitar. Scene regular Skizz Cyzyk is the one remembering the Baltimore reaction.
years.xp:
The Maryland Center for History and Culture dates Kohl's photo to about 1984, likely November 2, going by a Loyola student paper's mention of a Reptile House show with D.C.'s Grey Matter. The New Loft, at Mulberry and Eutaw, is described there as "a dark, dingy, smelly place."

A mainstream daily giving a full front page to a scene it mostly ignored was rare, which is why Cyzyk still remembered it.

eras.title: Two labels, one 7 inch
eras.text: Reptile House drove to Arlington to make their first real record, 4-Songs, with Ian MacKaye producing. It came out on Dischord and on the band's own Druid Hill label at the same time.

years.h: London May leaves for Glenn Danzig's Samhain
years.p: [[London May|57e0394c-afeb-4021-8193-940084dd4717]] joins [[Samhain|7991397c-2baf-49f3-8d73-c78e428825f8]], Danzig's post-[[Misfits|936addc3-91aa-49de-8ec0-0dc186de151f]] band, and plays on November-Coming-Fire. Gary Breezee is later listed on the Reptile House drum stool.
years.xp: Steven Blush's American Hardcore (2010) files Reptile House under the people it spawned: London May of Samhain and Dan Higgs of Lungfish.

years.src: Dischord · Maryland Center for History and Culture
years.h: Two labels share 4-Songs, Reptile House's debut 7"
years.p: Recorded at Inner Ear in March 1985 with [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] producing and [[Don Zientara|a495882b-4585-4295-9269-e30c63f279fe]] engineering, it came out in November on Dischord and the band's own Druid Hill. Collectors know it as I Stumble as the Crow Flies.
years.xp: The four songs are Keel Haul Love, Social Champion, Mrs. Rain and Sleestak Weather, with [[Leigh Panlilio|b24853ba-d025-4da6-b30f-5d1d5b09498b]] now on bass. London May has compared the sound to [[Flipper|4e99b3a5-654b-43ee-a9bf-c55c155c0495]]: mid-tempo rhythms and a noisy, jam-session feel, according to Wikipedia's account of his interviews.

eras.title: On the road, then out the door
eras.text: Reptile House toured as far as Detroit and Texas, per AllMusic, and headlined D.C.'s 9:30 Club. By the end Asa Osborne was on guitar, Listen to the Powersoul was out on Joe Goldsborough's Merkin label, and singer Daniel Strasser was about to become Daniel Higgs.

years.p: Dischord lists Osborne in later Reptile House lineups. It's the start of a partnership with Strasser, soon to be Higgs, that outlasts the band.

years.h: The only album comes out on Goldsborough's own label
years.p: Listen to the Powersoul is released on Merkin Records, which guitarist Joe Goldsborough runs, in fall 1988.

years.h: Strasser takes the name Higgs and starts Lungfish
years.p: Soon after Listen to the Powersoul, the singer leaves, becomes Daniel Higgs, and forms [[Lungfish|5af88bca-9c13-424a-b63c-b5c96c69cb0e]] with Osborne. Reptile House recruits Grey March keyboardist Ron Weldon to sing, then breaks up.

years.h: Goldsborough turns to psychedelic pop with the Ultra Violets
years.p: The guitarist forms the band with Reptile House bassist Joey Cirri, then uses Merkin to document the Baltimore underground into the '90s.

eras.title: Twenty-five years on
eras.text: By 2010 Daniel Higgs had spent two decades fronting Lungfish on Dischord. The label went back to where he started and reissued the first Reptile House record for its 25th anniversary.

years.p: The 1985 7" returns as Dischord 15.75, announced alongside reissues from Dag Nasty, Artificial Peace and Government Issue. Wikipedia says it had never been on CD in its original form.
years.xp: Wikipedia credits MacKaye and London May with putting the reissue together, and gives November 8, 2010 as the release date. Dischord's own release page says November 16, so the card says November.

years.h: Goldsborough plays guitar in Gag School
years.p: Kenny Sanders, Ken Mosher and Joe LaVoie are the rest of the band, per Wikipedia.
